correctness.rationale: In a connected chain graph, a minimum-neighborhood vertex of \(A\) has neighborhood exactly the universal twin class \(B^\star\), and symmetrically on the other side. Thus every total dominating set must meet both \(A^\star\) and \(B^\star\); conversely one selected universal vertex on each side dominates the entire graph. The same pair connects every selected vertex, so every total dominating set is automatically connected total dominating. Independent subset choices on the two sides yield the product polynomial. Factoring powers of \(1+x\) gives the root multiset and the real-root criterion. The bundled exhaustive checker verifies the set criterion, connectivity and coefficient formula on all canonical connected chain graphs in its bounded range.
residual_risks: The theorem assumes connected chain graphs; disconnected graphs with isolates fall outside the scope.

value.rationale: Chain graphs are a standard structured bipartite class and total/connected-total domination polynomials are natural enumerative invariants. The exact iff set classification, coincidence of the two domination notions, closed factorization and complete root geometry form a useful structural theorem beyond the known complete-bipartite special case.
